translation.title: The Overwhelming
notes: English translation of the Arabic text in the source file. Structure, unit numbers, ayah ranges, volume/page/serial numbers are unchanged.
Each segment keeps the page boundary of the original, so a sentence may break mid-way between segments, as it does in the printed edition.
Chains of transmission (isnad) are translated literally as 'X told us, he said: Y told us, from Z'. Names are transliterated.

Qur'anic quotations are given in braces in a plain English rendering that follows al-Tabari's reading of the verse. Arabic terms that are the subject of discussion (e.g. dari', shibriq, ghashiyah) are transliterated.
Editor's footnotes are translated; abbreviations of manuscript/print witnesses (ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3) are kept as in the original.
Bracketed text [ ] is the editor's own addition, as in the source.

x: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Commentary on Surah al-Ghashiyah (The Overwhelming).
Discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Mighty is His praise:

Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming (1) Faces on that Day will be humbled (2) laboring, weary (3) entering a scorching Fire (4) given to drink from a boiling spring (5) They will have no food except from a bitter thorny plant, dari' (6) which neither nourishes nor avails against hunger (7)
He, exalted be His mention, says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him:
? That is: its story and its news.
The scholars of interpretation differed over the meaning of 'the Overwhelming' (al-Ghashiyah).
Some said: It is the Resurrection, which overwhelms people with terrors.
Mention of those who said this:

c: 'Ali told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas:
m: 'The Overwhelming' is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection; God magnified it and warned His servants of it

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada,
m: Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming
. He said: The Overwhelming is the Hour

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas,

x: Others said: Rather, the Overwhelming is the Fire, which covers the faces of the disbelievers.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ash'ath, from Sa'id,
m: Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming
. The correct view on this is to say: God said to His Prophet, peace be upon him:
Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming
? He did not inform us that He meant the overwhelming of the Resurrection, nor that He meant the overwhelming of the Fire, and both are 'overwhelming': the former overwhelms people with distress

, and the latter overwhelms the disbelievers with the scorching blast in the face, with flame and molten brass. So there is no statement more sound than to say it as God, Mighty is His praise, said it, and to leave the report general just as He made it general.

x: Faces on that Day will be humbled
. He, exalted be His mention, says:
, and they are the faces of the people who disbelieved in Him,
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada:
m: Faces on that Day will be humbled

c: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada,
m: . He said: Humbled in the Fire

x: . That is: laboring in the Fire.
The scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas:
m: : they labor and toil in the Fire

c: Ya'qub told me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, from Abu Raja', he said:
m: . He said: They did not labor for God in the world, so He made them labor in the Fire

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada:
m: : they were arrogant in the world toward obedience to God, so He made them labor and toil in the Fire

c: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada,
m: . He said: Laboring and weary in the Fire (1).

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying:
. He said: No one is more weary, or more afflicted, than the people of the Fire.

x: . He, exalted be His mention, says: These faces will come to a scorching Fire, which has become hot and whose heat has grown intense. The readers differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited
with a fatha on the ta', meaning: the faces will enter (the Fire). Abu 'Amr recited (tusla) with a damma on the ta', taking it in parallel with His saying:
given to drink from a boiling spring
. The position on this is that both are valid readings with sound meaning, so whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct.

evidence.text: The readers differed in the recitation of this.
The majority of the readers of Kufa recited {tasla} with a fatha on the ta', meaning: the faces will enter (the Fire).

x: given to drink from a boiling spring
. He says: The people of these faces will be given to drink from the water of a spring whose heat has reached its limit ('ana), attaining the utmost extreme of heat.
The scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas,
m: given to drink from a boiling spring
. He said: It is one whose boiling has lasted long

c: Ya'qub told me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan,
m: given to drink from a boiling spring
: Its boiling has reached its term

c: Ya'qub related it to me
m: another time and said: Since the day God created the heavens and the earth

c: Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, on God's saying:
. He said: It has reached its time (ina), and the time for drinking it has come

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada,
m: given to drink from a boiling spring
. He says: Its boiling has reached its term since God created the heavens and the earth

c: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan,
m: . He said: From a spring whose heat has reached its term. He says: Its heat has reached its limit

x: Some said that what is meant by
Mention of those who said this:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying:
given to drink from a boiling spring

x: They will have no food except from a bitter thorny plant, dari'
. He says: Those who are the owners of the

humbled, laboring, weary faces will have no food on the Day of Resurrection except what they eat from dari'. Among the Arabs, dari' is a plant called shibriq. The people of the Hijaz call it dari' when it dries, while others call it shibriq, and it is a poison.
The scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas:
m: They will have no food except from dari'

c: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi told me, he said: 'Abbad ibn Ya'qub al-Asadi told us
m: - Muhammad said 'told us', while 'Abbad said 'informed us' - Muhammad ibn Sulayman informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Asbahani, from 'Ikrima, on His saying:
They will have no food except from dari'

c: Ya'qub told me, he said: Isma'il ibn 'Ulayya told us, from Abu Raja', he said:
m: Najda, a man of 'Abd al-Qays, told me, from 'Ikrima, on His saying:
They will have no food except from dari'
. He said: It is a thorny tree that lies flat on the ground; when it is spring the Quraysh call it shibriq, and when the stalk dries out they call it dari'

c: Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, from Layth, from Mujahid:
m: They will have no food except from dari'

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid,
Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, on His saying:

c: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada:
m: . He said: It is shibriq; when it dries it is called dari'

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada,
m: They will have no food except from dari'
. He says: From the worst, most loathsome and foulest of foods

c: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd told me, he said: Sharik ibn 'Abd Allah told us,
m: They will have no food except from dari'

x: Mention of those who said this:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id,
m: They will have no food except from dari'

x: Others said: Dari' is a tree of fire.
Mention of those who said this:

c: 'Ali told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas,
m: They will have no food except from dari'
. He says: A tree of fire

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying:
They will have no food except from dari'
. He said: Dari' is thorn from the Fire. He said: As for the world, dari' is dry thorn that has no leaves, which the Arabs call dari', and in the Hereafter it is a thorn of fire

x: which neither nourishes nor avails against hunger
. He says: This dari' will not fatten those of the people of the Fire who eat it on the Day of Resurrection,
. He says: nor will it satisfy them against the hunger that afflicts them.
Discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted:

Faces on that Day will be joyful (8) pleased with their endeavor (9) in an elevated Garden (10) wherein you will hear no idle speech (11) Within it is a flowing spring (12) Within it are couches raised high (13) and cups set in place (14) and cushions arranged in rows (15) and carpets spread around (16)
He, exalted be His mention, says:
. That is, the Day of Resurrection,
. He says: They are joyful through God's bestowing of bliss on their people in His gardens, and they are the people of faith in God.
. He says: pleased with their deeds that they did in the world in obedience to their Lord. It was also said:
, and the meaning is: pleased with the reward of their endeavor in the Hereafter.
wherein you will hear no idle speech

. He says: These faces will not hear - the meaning being: its people will not hear in it, in the elevated Garden - any 'laghiya'. By 'laghiya' He means a word of idle talk (laghw). Laghw is falsehood, so the word that is idle talk was called 'laghiya', just as one who has a coat of mail is called 'dari'', one who has a horse 'faris', and one who composes poetry 'sha'ir'. And as al-Hutay'a said
: 'You deceived me and claimed that you are a purveyor of milk in summer, and of dates' - meaning: an owner of milk and an owner of dates. One of the Kufan grammarians
claimed that the meaning is: no one swearing falsely will be heard

in it, and for that reason it was called 'laghiya'. This view of his has a basis and a rationale, were it not that the people of interpretation among the Companions and Followers held otherwise, and it is not permissible for anyone to contradict them in what they were unanimous upon.
The scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas,
m: wherein you will hear no idle speech
. He says: You will hear no harm and no falsehood

c: Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, on His saying:
wherein you will hear no idle speech

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada,
m: wherein you will hear no idle speech
: You will hear in it no falsehood and no abuser.

c: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada,
m: . The readers differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Kufa, and some of the readers of Medina, namely Abu Ja'far, recited
with a fatha on the ta', meaning: the faces will not hear
. Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Abu 'Amr recited (la tusma'u) with a damma on the ta', in the passive form, with 'tusma'' being feminine because 'laghiya' is feminine
. Ibn Muhaysin also recited it with a damma, except that he read it with a ya', in the masculine form
. In my view, the correct position on this is that all of these are well-known readings with sound meanings, so whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct.

evidence.text: The readers differed in the recitation of this.
The majority of the readers of Kufa, and some of the readers of Medina, namely Abu Ja'far, recited {la tasma'u} with a fatha on the ta', meaning: the faces will not hear (4).
Ibn Muhaysin also recited it with a damma, except that he read it with a ya', in the masculine form (6).

x: Within it is a flowing spring
. He says: In the elevated Garden is a spring that flows without a channel (ukhdud).
Within it are couches raised high

. 'Sururun' is the plural of 'sarir' (couch). They are raised so that the believer, when he sits upon them, may see everything his Lord has granted him of bliss and dominion in it, his sight reaching all of it. It was also said that what is meant by
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas:
m: Within it are couches raised high
. He means: woven, like His saying:

x: . 'Akwab' is the plural of 'kub', which are the pitchers without handles. We have already explained this earlier and mentioned the reports on it, which makes repeating it unnecessary
is that they are set at the edge of the flowing spring, so that whenever he wishes to drink he finds them
. By 'namariq' He means pillows and armrests
, the singular of which is 'numruqa', with a damma on the nun. It has also been reported, as heard from some of Kalb, 'nimriqa', with a kasra on the nun and the ra'. It was said
because some of them are beside others.
The scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: 'Ali told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas,
Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas,
Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada,
m: : and the namariq are the pillows

x: . He, exalted be His mention, says: And in it are many rugs and mats, spread around and laid out. The singular is 'zarbiyya', which is a rug with a fine nap.
The scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Ahmad ibn Mansur told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: [Sufyan told us
m: , he said: Tawba al-'Anbari told us, from 'Ikrima ibn Khalid, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ammar, he said: I saw 'Umar ibn al-Khattab praying on an 'abqari, which is the zarabi.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada:

x: Discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted:
Then do they not look at the camels, how they are created (17) and at the sky, how it is raised (18) and at the mountains, how they are erected (19) and at the earth, how it is spread out (20)

He, exalted be His mention, says to those who deny His power over what He described in this surah of the punishment and retribution He has prepared for the people of enmity toward Him, and the bliss and honor He has prepared for the people of His friendship: Do these deniers of God's power over these things not look at the camels, how He created them, subjected them to them, made them docile, and made them carry their loads while kneeling and then rise with them? The One who created that finds it no hard matter to create what He described of these things in the Garden and the Fire. The Mighty is His praise says: Do they not look at the camels, and so take a lesson from them, and know that the power by which He was able to create them [will not fail Him]
in creating the like of them?
The scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, he said:
m: When God described what is in the Garden, the people of misguidance were astonished at it, so God sent down:
Then do they not look at the camels, how they are created
. The camels were part of the livelihood of the Arabs and of their property

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, he said: Shu'ba told us
m: , from Abu Ishaq, from one who heard Shurayh saying: Come out with us so that we may look at the camels, how they were created

x: and at the sky, how it is raised
. He, Mighty is His praise, says: Do they not also look at the sky above them

, how it was raised by the One who informed you that He has prepared for His friends what He described and for His enemies what He mentioned, so that they may know that His power is a power that nothing He wills to do can overpower?
and at the mountains, how they are erected
. He says: And at the mountains, how they were set up upright, so that they do not fall and spread flat upon the earth, [but]
He, by His power, made them upright and solid, never leaving their place and never shifting from their position.

c: Bishr also told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada:
m: and at the mountains, how they are erected

for most of your day, and when you reach its summit, you reach gushing springs and hanging fruits there, which no hands have tilled and no one has worked, a blessing from God, and a provision until the appointed term

x: and at the earth, how it is spread out
. He says: And at the earth, how it was laid out. One says: a 'musattah' mountain, when its top is level.
The scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada:
m: and at the earth, how it is spread out
. That is: laid out. He says: Is not the One who created this able to create whatever He wills in the Garden? (1)

x: Discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted:

So remind, you are only a reminder (21) you are not over them a controller (22) except he who turns away and disbelieves (23) then God will punish him with the greatest punishment (24) Indeed, to Us is their return (25) then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning (26)
He, exalted be His mention, says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him:
, Muhammad, My servants with My signs, admonish them with My proofs, and convey to them My message;
. He says: I sent you to them only as a reminder, to remind them of My favors toward them, to make known to them what is incumbent upon them, and to admonish them.
you are not over them a controller

. He says: You are not set in authority over them, nor are you a tyrant who forces them to what you wish. He says: Entrust them to Me, leave them and My judgment concerning them. One says: 'Fulan has taken control (tasaytara) over his people,' when he has gained dominion over them.
The scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: 'Ali told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas,
m: you are not over them a controller
. He says: You are not a tyrant over them

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada:
m: you are not over them a controller
. That is: Entrust My servants to Me

c: Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, on His saying:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying:
you are only a reminder (21) you are not over them a controller
. He said: You are not set in authority over them to compel them to believe. He said: Then after this came:
Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them
and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush
[al-Tawba: 5] - and lie in wait for them so that they do not go about in the land -
but if they repent and establish prayer and give zakat, let them go their way; indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful
you are not over them a controller
. He said: There came: kill him, or he accepts Islam. He said: And the reminding stays as it is, it was not abrogated. And he recited:
And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers

c: Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no god but God. When they say: There is no god but God, they secure from me their blood and their property, except by its right, and their reckoning is with God.” Then he recited:
you are only a reminder (21) you are not over them a controller

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Zubayr Muhammad ibn Muslim, he said:
m: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say, and he mentioned the like of it, except that he said: Abu al-Zubayr said: Then he recited:
you are only a reminder (21) you are not over them a controller

c: Yusuf ibn Musa al-Qattan told us, he said: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of God,
m: peace and blessings be upon him, the like of it.

x: except he who turns away and disbelieves
. This can be taken in two ways. One: Remind your people, Muhammad, except for the one among them who turns away from you and turns aside from God's signs and disbelieves. Then His saying

is an exception from those upon whom the reminding was incumbent, even though they were not (in fact) reminded, as one might say: 'So-and-so went off and called (people), except those whose response is not hoped for,' meaning: he called the people except those whose response is not hoped for. The second way: that His saying
except he who turns away and disbelieves

is made disconnected from what precedes it. The meaning of the speech is then: You are not a controller over them; but whoever turns away and disbelieves, God will punish him. The disconnected exception is tested by whether 'inna' (indeed) fits after it: if it fits, it is disconnected, and if it does not fit, it is a sound connected exception, as in a speaker's words: 'The people travelled, except Zayd.' Inserting 'inna' here is not appropriate, because it is a sound (connected) exception
then God will punish him with the greatest punishment
, which is the punishment of Hell. He says: God will punish him with the greatest punishment for his disbelief in Him
with the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter.
Indeed, to Us is their return
Indeed, to Us is the return of the one who disbelieved, and their place of return,
then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning
. He says: Then upon God is his reckoning, and He will requite him for his past disobedience to his Lord.

By this He informs His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that He is the One who will take charge of his punishment, not him; that He is the Requiter and the Punisher; and that to him belongs the reminding and the conveying of the message.
The scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, on His saying:
except he who turns away and disbelieves
. He said: His reckoning is with God

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada:
m: Indeed, to Us is their return (25) then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning
. He says: To God is the return, and upon Him is the reckoning
. End of the commentary on Surah al-Ghashiyah.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim, as cited in al-Itqān, 2/55, reported it through Abū Ṣāliḥ. Ibn Kathīr cites it briefly in his Tafsīr, 8/406.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم - كما في الإتقان 2/ 55 - من طريق أبي صالح به، وذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 406، مختصرا عند كليهما.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributes it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 6/342, to al-Muṣannaf, ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 342 إلى المصنف وعبد الرزاق وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributes it to al-Muṣannaf in al-Durr al-manthūr, 6/342.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 342 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Cited by al-Ṭūsī in al-Tibyān, 10/334; al-Qurṭubī in his Tafsīr, 20/25; and Abū Ḥayyān in al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 8/462.
notes.ar: ذكره الطوسى في التبيان 10/ 334، والقرطبي في تفسيره 20/ 25، وأبو حيان في البحر المحيط 8/ 462.

notes.en: M and T1 read “with affliction.” Balābil means intense worry. See Lisān al-ʿArab, root (ب ل ل).
notes.ar: في م، ت 1: "بالبلاء". والبلابل: شدَّة الهَمّ. ينظر اللسان (ب ل ل).
